findings.title: Per-row Python loop in _comfort_terms_batch costs 13-32% of every solve; a row-vectorized twin is bit-identical here
findings.claim: HeatPumpOptimizer._comfort_terms_batch spends 0.134-0.321 of optimize() thread CPU (0.32 on every two-zone cell) in a per-row numpy loop, and a twin that does the same elementwise ops on the [B, n] batch and reduces with axis=1 returns bitwise-identical penalty and comfort arrays and the same plans on all 8 cells tested, at 0.012-0.039 of the solve.
findings.mechanism: The batched gradient's 96 rows each re-enter ~11 np.sum plus ~10 elementwise numpy calls (two-zone) on 96-element arrays, so per-call Python/ufunc dispatch overhead, not arithmetic, is the cost: 501 gradient batches x 96 rows on the default two-zone DHW winter cell. The docstring keeps the loop for cross-backend bit parity; the measured twin gives 0 bit mismatches on x86_64, which is where the docstring says a batched reduction re-planned 19 of 51 stress scenarios.

findings.title: L-BFGS-B asks the scalar objective for f(x) every iterate at ~19-26x a batched row: 9-19% of the solve
findings.claim: _multi_start_minimize hands scipy a scalar fun and a batched jac separately, so every iterate evaluates the scalar objective (1.0-1.6 ms, 18.6-25.9x one batched row) before the 96-row gradient batch; that scalar path is 0.087-0.192 of optimize() thread CPU, and serving f from an extra row 0 of the same batch (jac=True) drops it to 0.005-0.018 with every plan bitwise unchanged.
findings.mechanism: scipy's ScalarFunction calls fun(x) then jac(x); the memo (#288) only saves the jac's f0 re-evaluation, not the scalar evaluation itself, which runs simulate_trajectory as a Python loop of simulate_step with a dataclasses.replace per step. The batched kernel's cost is per-call overhead amortised over rows, so a 97th row costs ~0.04-0.08 ms where the scalar call costs 1.0-1.6 ms. A one-row batch per scalar call is dearer still (recorded negative arm --via-batch: share 0.15 -> 0.31).

findings.title: DHW min-run repair: a full-suffix re-simulation per refused weak slot, 12-23% of a single-zone DHW solve
findings.claim: _apply_dhw_min_run makes 7,758 of the solve's 11,064 simulate_dhw_step calls on the single-zone DHW winter cell (0.17-0.23 of optimize() CPU on four single-zone cells), 81 % of its weak slots are refused, and stopping each refused slot's check at its first breaching chunk cuts the calls 26-40 % (7,758 -> 4,780) with every plan bitwise unchanged; at 48 h the calls grow 3.26x for 2x the horizon.
findings.mechanism: Each weak slot extends the candidate trajectory from the slot to the end of the horizon (#1230's prefix reuse), and a refused slot then re-extends the base from the slot again, so the loop is O(weak x (n - slot)) Python steps; the refusal decision is already known at the first step that breaches.

findings.title: Euler sub-step guard judges each store's diagonal ratio only, so coupled stores in accepted configs diverge
findings.claim: For configurations the config flow accepts, ThermalModel._stability_substeps leaves the per-substep Euler map with spectral radius > 1, and a zero-input 24 h trajectory diverges (69/3936 grid configs leave the passive envelope, 50 past 100 K; named point reaches -2.84e35 degC).
findings.mechanism: _stability_substeps bounds each store's (sum of couplings)/C*h by EULER_STABILITY_MAX_RATIO=1.5, on the premise that Euler is stable up to 2 per store. For coupled RC stores the stiff eigenvalue reaches the sum of the diagonal terms (Gershgorin: |lambda| <= 2*max diag), so lambda*h reaches 3 and the update oscillates with growth. Example: house mass 0.5, loss 0.2, slab mass 0.5, slab transfer 5.0 -> n_sub=2, radius 1.525.

findings.title: DHW refill coil debits the wood tank the full coil heat but spares the DHW tank only its scaled share
findings.claim: In simulate_trajectory_with_dhw with the wood coil active, for a DHW tank below DHW_MIXED_USE_TEMP, the wood tank loses more heat than the coil spares the DHW tank (non-zero in 28/28 cells, up to 0.406 kWh per 15-min step; 0.054 kWh at DHW 35 degC / wood 70 degC).
findings.mechanism: dhw_coil_draw_reduction splits the nominal draw into reduced+coil==draw and the wood tank is debited coil. simulate_dhw_step then scales the reduced draw by min(1,(T-inlet)/(40-inlet)), so the DHW tank is spared only scale*coil. (1-scale)*coil vanishes per step. The tap water is the same with or without the coil, because the coil only preheats the refill.

findings.title: A malformed weather-forecast response wedges every later cycle until restart
findings.claim: One weather.get_forecasts response whose forecast holds a non-dict row or is not a list makes every later _async_update_data raise UpdateFailed, even after the weather entity returns a healthy forecast again.

leads.what: Substep count grows without bound with the wind-driven heat loss: one forecast step at wind 1e12 m/s makes a solve run past 60 s (1e6 finishes in 0.9 s). A cap on n_sub (or on the wind it is computed from) would bound a runaway solve whatever the coordinator passes (see D1-s2-02).

Scrubs non-finite leaves but passes finite values that become unrepresentable after the loader's int() (>= 2**64 floats); the store boundary could refuse counts beyond int64 for every store at once (see D1-s2-03).

Parses with stdlib json, which accepts NaN/Infinity tokens and >64-bit integers that Home Assistant's orjson-based Store refuses (whole file quarantined). Fuzz results through the stub include failures that cannot occur in HA; energy 10**400 and defrost duty 10**400 were two.

Calls each async_on_unload callback synchronously and drops a returned coroutine (RuntimeWarning: coroutine 'HeatPumpOptimizerCoordinator.async_shutdown' was never awaited, registered by the stub DataUpdateCoordinator); Home Assistant awaits coroutine unload callbacks.
